stream.title: Jamming at zero temperature and zero applied stress: The epitome of disorder
stream.venue: Physical review. E, Statistical physics, plasmas, fluids, and related interdisciplinary topics
stream.hypothesis: Confine a compliant medium around the object, then drive it past a jamming transition so the assembly goes from fluid-like to load-bearing. One global signal, no per-object programming.
stream.source_passage: At low packing fractions phi, the system is not jammed and each particle can move without impediment from its neighbors. For each configuration, there is a unique jamming threshold phi(c) at which particles can no longer avoid each other, and the bulk and shear moduli simultaneously become nonzero.

mapping.home_concept: Gripper switching from compliant to rigid
Load-bearing contact network around the object

stream.reviewer_note: Holding force depends on friction and confinement, so very smooth, heavy or delicate objects are likely harder. Expect failure on polished or high-friction surfaces.

stream.title: Jamming phase diagram for attractive particles
stream.hypothesis: Use the same stiffening transition with attractive rather than repulsive particles, which widens the range of shapes that can be held.
stream.source_passage: A wide variety of systems, including granular media, colloidal suspensions and molecular systems, exhibit non-equilibrium transitions from a fluid-like to a solid-like state, characterized solely by the sudden arrest of their dynamics. Crowding or jamming of the constituent particles traps them kinetically, precluding further exploration of the phase space.

mapping.home_concept: Passive grip that grips harder as it is squeezed

mapping.source_concept: Phase diagram in density vs. attraction
mapping.home_concept: Operating envelope over object size and softness

stream.reviewer_note: Attractive particles introduce a cohesive mode where the gripper can retain an object without applied vacuum. Not obviously robust to particulate contamination.

stream.title: Jamming, Force Chains, and Fragile Matter
stream.hypothesis: Once rigid, the load is carried by a sparse contact network, so the design target is the strength of that network rather than the medium.
stream.source_passage: We argue that such media are generically ``fragile,'' unable to support certain types of incremental loading without plastic rearrangement. Fragility is linked to the marginal stability of force chain networks within the material.

mapping.home_concept: Which contacts carry load and which fail first

stream.reviewer_note: Fragility is the concern: a small number of contacts carries most of the load, so localised damage may cause sudden loss of grip rather than a graceful degradation.
